curriculum.lesson_evidence: Wheels and axles reduce friction for moving loads; ramps (inclined planes) let us raise loads with less steep effort over a longer distance.

lesson.child_mission: Wheels and axles reduce friction for moving loads; ramps (inclined planes) let us raise loads with less steep effort over a longer distance.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same science idea to a new object or material, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Which helps more for a heavy box into a ute tray: a steep short lift or a longer gentle ramp? Explain simply.

FEEDBACK
Longer gentle ramp usually needs less effort force (over more distance).

WATCH FOR
Thinking ramps “create free energy” is false — you trade force for distance.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Test rolling vs dragging a mass and ramp vs lift (safe masses). Record effort observations and one labelled diagram each.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.

Wheels and axles reduce friction for moving loads; ramps (inclined planes) let us raise loads with less steep effort over a longer distance.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.
